title: Per-route policy loom: automated tiering, allowlist/denylist synthesis and safe rollback harness
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Build an automated per-route/per-customer policy generation and safe-apply harness (the 'policy loom') that produces suggested batching and KV-cache configurations, synthesizes allowlists/denylists based on request characteristics and SLAs, and provides an automated staged apply + deterministic rollback path.

Scope:
- Inference of candidate tier assignments (e.g., gold/silver/bronze) per customer-route using historical telemetry (latency, cost-per-token, error rate).
- Generate recommended batching and prefix/KV-cache parameters per tier and per route, including confidence scores and expected cost delta.
- Produce allowlist/denylist suggestions for aggressive optimizations (e.g., long-batch-safe routes) and a soft-deny classification to avoid hard failures.
- Implement a dry-run simulator that predicts latency and cost with synthetic workloads and replays for top-k customers.
- Safe-apply orchestration: staged canary deployment with automatic metrics gating and deterministic rollback triggers (SLO breach, error spike, customer-specific anomaly).
- Operator UI hooks: expose recommendations, rationale, confidence, and one-click stage/cancel controls in the Console rollout UI (design spec link below).

Deliverables:
1) Policy synthesizer service that emits JSON policy bundles: tier assignment, batching params, cache presets, allowlist/denylist candidates, and telemetry hooks.
2) Dry-run simulator and replay harness wired into the stage pipeline.
3) Safe-apply orchestrator with metrics gates, circuit breaker, and rollback hooks.
4) Runbook and automated postmortem checklist for failed applies.

Acceptance criteria:
- Synthesizer evaluates historical data and produces recommendations for 90% of active routes with confidence score >= 0.6.
- Dry-run predictions for cost delta and p95 latency within 15% of observed results in a subsequent staged canary.
- Canary gating rollbacks automatically trigger when any of the defined SLOs (latency p95, error rate, token throughput) exceed configured thresholds for 10 minutes.
- Operators can approve/reject suggestions in the Console and see attribution to telemetry signals.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- We will prioritize high-traffic routes for first rollout to maximize unit-cost impact; long-tail routes default to conservative safe profiles.
- Allowlist/denylist synthesis will start with deterministic heuristics (payload size, sequence length distribution, call frequency, presence of streaming) and evolve to a lightweight xGBoost classifier for edge cases.
- Conservative defaults: synthesized denylist entries become "soft denies" (optimization skipped but instrumented) until manually promoted after confirmation.
- Risk: Overaggressive batching can increase tail latency for latency-sensitive customers. Mitigations: per-route latency SLOs, sample-level traces during canary, and automatic rollback.

Telemetry & metrics:
- Inputs: per-token cost, p50/p90/p95 latency, error rate, sequence length histogram, request frequency, model variant.
- Outputs: predicted cost delta, projected latency delta, confidence score, applied policy id, canary result metrics.
- Dashboards: rollout dashboard will include pre/post cost/latency comparison, top affected customers, and diffed trace samples.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal simulation and dry-run on staging (2 weeks).
2) Small canary: 5 routes representing different traffic patterns (1 week).
3) Expand to top-50 routes by QPS with automated gating (2 weeks).
4) Gradual broader rollout with operator approvals for medium and low traffic routes.

Observability & debugging:
- Attach correlation IDs to policy bundles; store policy application events in the event log for retrospective queries.
- Add lightweight traces around batching entrance/exit and KV cache hit/miss breakdown.
- Capture sample payloads for failed canary intervals for offline replay.

Runbook (high-level):
- Pre-checks: ensure latest runtime-1.20 staging image is available; smoke test.
- Start canary: create policy bundle, enable dry-run, push to canary lanes (5 routes).
- Monitor gating metrics for 30 minutes; if thresholds breached, flip circuit and rollback via orchestrator endpoint.
- Postmortem: auto-generate incident draft with metric diffs and sample traces.

Links to artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/x/PolicyLoomDesign
- Dry-run simulator prototype (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-loom/tree/prototype/dryrun
- Console rollout mockups (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Policy-Loom-Rollout

Notes for reviewers:
- Need feedback on confidence thresholding heuristics and initial set of SLO gates.
- Input wanted from product on customer tier mapping rules and any customers that must be excluded from automated policies (compliance/contractual).
